results.name: Band Bent-Over Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, ensuring it is secure. Hold one handle of the band in each hand with your palms facing each other, bending your torso forward at the hips while keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor, fully extended, with your elbows slightly bent.
Pull the handles towards your torso by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you pull the band towards your torso and inhale as you lower it back down.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Band Bent-Over Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Band Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight down, palms facing your hips.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees, keeping your back straight, lowering your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor.
Press through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand back up straight, bringing the handles up along your legs until you are fully upright.
Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you lower back down.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
results.description: Band Deadlift is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Band Kneeling Single Arm High Row
instructions: Attach a loop resistance band to a sturdy anchor point above head height. Kneel on your right knee, with the opposite foot flat on the ground for balance. Hold one end of the band with your right arm and keep it fully extended.
Pull the band down towards your torso by bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your arm fully while maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Use a controlled motion to pull and release the band, avoiding jerking movements.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the band and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blade at the top of the movement to maximize back activation.
results.description: Band Kneeling Single Arm High Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Rear Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Band Pull Up
instructions: Securely loop a resistance band around a pull-up bar. Place one or both feet into the bottom of the loop band. Grip the pull-up bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, palms facing forward.
Start in a dead hang position with your arms fully extended.
Pull yourself upward by bending your elbows and driving them down towards your sides, bringing your chin above the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Adjust the resistance band to match your strength level. Thicker bands provide more assistance.
Avoid using momentum; focus on pulling with your back and arms.
results.description: Band Pull Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Bent Over Row Pronate Grip
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands in a pronated grip (palms facing backward), and your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Slightly bend your knees, and hinge at your hips to lower your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your back straight and your gaze forward.
Pull the barbell towards your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement. Keeping your elbows close to your body.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid rounding your back by keeping your chest up and your spine neutral.
Move the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Bent Over Row Pronate Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Bent Over Row Supinated Grip
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands in a supinated grip (palms facing forward), and your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Slightly bend your knees, and hinge at your hips to lower your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your back straight and your gaze forward.
Pull the barbell towards your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement. Keeping your elbows close to your body.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid rounding your back by keeping your chest up and your spine neutral.
Move the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Bent Over Row Supinated Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Clean Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out, with a barbell on the floor in front of you. Bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core, keep your back straight, and your chest up. Begin the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor.
As the barbell passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and knees while shrugging your shoulders to bring the barbell to your upper thighs.
Reverse the movement by lowering the barbell back to the floor with control, maintaining a straight back and engaged core. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine to avoid rounding your back and prevent injury.
Use your legs and hips to drive the barbell up, minimizing the strain on your lower back.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout the lift to maintain proper form.
results.description: Barbell Clean Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Coan Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward. Position a barbell over the middle of your feet, and squat down to grip the barbell with both hands inside your legs, using an overhand grip.
Brace your core and drive through your heels as you extend your knees and hips simultaneously, keeping the barbell close to your legs throughout the lift.
Stand fully upright squeezing your glutes at the top of the exercise. Keep your shoulders back, and the bar resting against your thighs.
Hinge at your hips first, then bend your knees to lower the barbell under control along the same path until it returns to the floor.
tips: Keep the barbell as close to your body as possible throughout the lift and avoid rounding your lower back.
Drive through your heels while extending your hips and keep your chest up.
Avoid jerking the bar from the floor during the beginning of the lift and lower the barbell in a controlled fashion while hinging at the hip joint.
Exhale as you complete the lift and inhale before beginning the next repetition.
results.description: Barbell Coan Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Lats, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Deadlift (360 Degree View)
instructions: Bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Begin the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor.
As the barbell passes your knees, continue to lift by extending your hips until you are standing upright with the barbell in front of your thighs.
Lower the barbell back to the floor with control by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, maintaining a straight back and engaged core. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your head in line with your spine to maintain proper neck alignment and prevent strain.
Visualize pulling the barbell back rather than up, to keep it close to your body and use the correct muscle groups.
Use a mixed grip (one hand overhand, one hand underhand) for heavier lifts to enhance grip strength.
results.description: Barbell Deadlift (360 Degree View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Deadlift High Pull
instructions: Place a barbell on the floor in front of you. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointed slightly outward.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower your body, grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.

Push through your heels to lift the barbell off the floor, extending your hips and knees simultaneously. As you reach the standing position, pull the barbell upward towards your chin by bending your elbows and keeping them pointed outward.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
Push through your heels to maximize power and stability.
Ensure your knees track over your toes to prevent knee strain.
results.description: Barbell Deadlift High Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Upper Back, Lower Back.
